narrative.overview: Kizuna Signal is an editorial intelligence instrument: quiet enough for consequential reading, precise enough for dense evidence, and memorable through one live spectral signal that represents evidence moving through the system. It is restrained rather than decorative; dense decision content is progressively disclosed without disguising uncertainty or unsupported capabilities.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial serif conclusions paired with neutral interface typography.
Flat mineral surfaces separated by rules instead of stacked shadows.
One spectral evidence rail as the recurring signature.
Monospaced labels for versions, measurements, and provenance.
Responsive reading order that preserves evidence before decoration.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: Semantic color must describe a state; it is never used as general decoration.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif communicates conclusions; sans and mono communicate interaction and evidence.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface can be separated by spacing, tone, or a hairline, it does not receive a shadow.

dos: Do show provenance, warnings, and scoring versions next to decision outputs.
Do use semantic color together with readable status text.
Do preserve large editorial moments around the score and final decision.
Do keep incomplete model and dataset capabilities explicitly labelled.
donts: Don't copy Octolane logos, proprietary copy, assets, or distinctive brand marks.
Don't turn every section into a floating card or use gradients as generic decoration.
Don't present confidence as prediction accuracy or public demand proxies as guaranteed revenue.
Don't label deterministic metadata or scoring as AI-generated until a real inference endpoint is connected.
